title: Toward Generalizable Evaluation in the LLM Era: A Survey Beyond Benchmarks

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing evaluations of LLM-as-a-judge systems that measure the tendency of models to favor answers based on their presentation order in the prompt, often evaluated and mitigated via swap-augmentation (shuffling answer order).

Reviewing evaluations of LLM evaluators that measure the tendency to assign higher scores to outputs that align with preferred writing styles, verbosity, or tones over actual content quality, assessed using style-control benchmark variants.
Reviewing evaluations of LLM judges that measure performance drops when models are evaluated on mismatched formats (e.g., fine-tuned without a reference but validated with one).
Reviewing evaluations that measure systemic failures when the knowledge required for an evaluation task exceeds the scope of the LLM judge's pre-training data.

Surveying multi-dimensional trustworthiness benchmarks (e.g., DecodingTrust, BIG-bench) that use multiple-choice questions and scenario-based interaction tests to evaluate holistic fairness and stereotype associations.
Surveying content safety and moderation benchmarks that specifically probe model outputs for toxicity, bias, and hate speech related to gender and sexuality domains.
